newsitem.title: SUDAN: Iran's Velayati in Sudan for Ugandan mediation.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Velayati in Sudan for Ugandan mediation.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati arrived in Khartoum on Wednesday and said he would discuss the dispute between Sudan and Uganda both in Khartoum and later in the Ugandan capital Kampala.

Iran mediated an agreement between the two African countries last September but it has had little effect on events on the Ugandan-Sudanese border, where the two sides continue to accuse each other of attacking in support of rebel groups.
Velayati said he had brought a written message for Sudanese President Hassan al-Bashir from Iranian President Ali Akbar Rafsanjani, Sudanese state radio said.
Sudanese Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha met Velayati at Khartoum airport, it added.
Asked about the Iranian mediation with Uganda, Velayati said: "The sides that signed the agreement have to keep whatever was agreed in the agreement." He did not elaborate.
Sudan says Uganda has attacked the southern border town of Kaya but Uganda says it is the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) that attacked.
The SPLA also claims responsibility for the attack and says its target is Juba, southern Sudan's main town.

The chairman of the foreign relations committee of the Sudanese parliament, Inayat Abdelhamid Inayat, was quoted on Tuesday as saying the aim of the attack in the south was to stop Iran trying to reconcile Khartoum and Kampala.
"Uganda wants to stop dialogue aimed at improving ties with Sudan and the attack is a message to Iran to stop its mediation," said Inayat, a former ambassador to Uganda.
